builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Cross-Provider Review as a Runtime Contract for Coding Agents: A Controlled Pilot and Fault-Injection Study
summary: The method replaces informal or absent second-opinion review of coding-agent output with a structured advisory contract spanning distinct provider resource pools, bounded execution, restricted reviewer capabilities, complete input delivery, and durable per-attempt evidence. It costs an additional API call from a separate subscription pool per reviewed turn, plus implementation and maintenance of the contract machinery; the pilot found substantive findings in only 8 of 20 paired turns, and some review calls yielded nothing useful. Fault injection exposed real failure modes: false success on truncated input, cancellation during process reaping, and a nonzero-exit reviewer with a well-formed verdict being counted as complete, the last of which invalidated the accrued 25-observation shadow-study cohort.
rationale: The pilot is small (20 paired turns), its measurement-valid cohort was restarted after a defect invalidated prior data, and no gate result is reported, so production adoption is premature though the contract pattern is worth tracking for teams already running multi-provider coding agents.
technique: Advisory cross-provider review contract for coding agents
